correctness.finding: PASS. The comb is a proper one-ended R-tree. Any escaping net of internal metric functionals eventually sees each fixed point through the spine and converges pointwise to the unique Busemann function b=r-p; any nonescaping subnet lies in a finite union of compact segments and yields an internal limit, giving the complete compactification. For fixed w, h_w(x_n)=n+L_n-2p(w) eventually, while b(x_n)=L_n-n, so the endpoint d-weak limit set is exactly the stated Busemann sublevel. The compact-range lemma is valid for nets by passing to a metric cluster subnet and testing against h_y. If L_n-n->-infinity, Busemann superlevels are bounded and properness forces every weakly convergent tail to converge metrically; if not, a subsequence has at least two distinct spine limits. At L_n=n the same sequence converges to every point, which indeed makes the topology hyperconnected, and the internal functional h_y separates singletons enough to give T1.
